newsitem.title: INDIA: Six guerrillas killed in Kashmir gun battle.
newsitem.headline: Six guerrillas killed in Kashmir gun battle.

text.p: Indian paramilitary troops killed at least six militants when they stormed the hide-out of a group of separatist guerrillas in troubled Jammu and Kashmir state, a defence spokesman said on Saturday.

The men were killed in a four-hour-long gunbattle late on Friday after troopers besieged their hide-out in the thickly forested Khag area, 40 kilometres south-west of Srinagar, the state's summer capital, spokesman Major P. Purshuttam said.
One trooper was injured in the exchange, Purshuttam said. He said he expected more bodies to be found.
"So far we have recovered six bodies from the encounter site," Purshuttam told Reuters. "Most of them are suspected foreigners. The toll can go higher."
More than 20,000 people have been killed in Kashmir after an Islamic separatist revolt broke out in 1990, according to official sources.
Since independence in 1947, India has fought two of its three wars with neighbouring Pakistan over Kashmir. It accuses Islamabad of arming and training the separatists.
Pakistan says it offers them only moral and diplomatic support.
